title: Joint laws from independent coordinate laws
statement: Let $I$ be a finite index set, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $(\Xi,\nu)$ be measurable probability spaces, and let $X_i:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ and $Y_i:\Xi\to\mathbb R$ be coordinate families. If each family is independent and corresponding coordinates have the same distribution, then the random vectors $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ and $(Y_i)_{i\in I}$ have the same distribution.
hypotheses_covered: The coordinate index set is finite
replaced: Let $I$ be a finite index set and let $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ and $(Y_i)_{i\in I}$ be real input families on probability spaces $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $(\Xi,\nu)$, respectively. If each family is independent and $X_i$ and $Y_i$ are measurable up to null sets with the same distribution for every $i$, then the random vectors $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ and $(Y_i)_{i\in I}$ have the same distribution.
